question: The length of a vertical rod and its shadow are in the ratio of 2 : √12. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Height** to **Shadow** = 2 : √12

Simplify ratio = 2 : 2√3 = 1 : √3

tan θ = Height ÷ Shadow = 1 / √3

Since tan 30° = 1 / √3, the **Angle of Elevation** is 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of length of **Rod** (AB) to **Shadow** (BC) = 2 : √12

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular (AB) ÷ Base (BC)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b34b11561ab7a680cf84c8b4dad73de3b3a749a7b32ad01b5be7694fee939ef.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan θ = 2 / √12

⇒ tan θ = 2 / √(4 × 3)

⇒ tan θ = 2 / (2√3)

⇒ tan θ = 1 / √3

⇒ θ = tan−¹(1 / √3)

⇒ θ = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values for tan θ are tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed **above** the horizontal level.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².</p
